sources.title: 2025 Annual Report, Chapter IV.B: Nicaragua
sources.temporal_coverage: Country conditions and cited events through 2025; climate impacts include El Niño conditions in 2024.
sources.methodology: IACHR Nicaragua chapter; full PDF inspected.
sources.limitations: Synthesis cites WFP/FAO/WMO; Dry Corridor only, without municipalities or event attribution.

sources.title: Violencia contra pueblos indígenas y afrodescendientes de la Costa Caribe en Nicaragua
sources.temporal_coverage: Historical violence and institutional developments through 2024; report approved 25 August 2025.
sources.methodology: Original 133-page Spanish IACHR thematic report inspected in full.
sources.limitations: The report documents rights and violence, not climate-event impacts; its climate connection concerns radio coverage of local environmental and climate issues.

sources.title: Nicaragua realizó el lanzamiento del Sistema Nacional de Respuesta a Emergencia de Nicaragua (SINAREM)
sources.organization: Sistema Nacional para la Prevención, Mitigación y Atención de Desastres (SINAPRED)
sources.temporal_coverage: SINAREM launch and design announcement, February 2025.
sources.methodology: Full official SINAPRED announcement page opened.
sources.limitations: Government announcement describes intended functions and launch, not operational reach or independently evaluated effectiveness.

sources.title: Nicaragua country strategic plan (2024–2029), Revision 02
sources.temporal_coverage: Strategic plan for 2024–2029; Revision 02 approved September 2026.
sources.methodology: WFP publisher page and its substantive plan and outcome summary inspected.
sources.limitations: The linked plan PDF returned an anti-robot challenge; page summary records commitments, not delivered outcomes, and gives no local target areas.

claims.paraphrase: IACHR identifies Nicaragua’s Dry Corridor as 63 municipalities (37% of territory), reliant partly on subsistence/small-scale farming; 2024 El Niño intensified drought and reduced rain, harming crop output and food security.
claims.limitations: No municipal rates or event attribution.
claims.source_stated_fcv_link: Para. 75 situates climate impacts within closure of civic and democratic space; para. 76 notes displacement and worsened access to basic resources.

claims.paraphrase: In the Dry Corridor, below-average and erratic rain reduced production and deepened household food insecurity; vulnerable families reduced food quantity or quality and withdrew children from school.
affected_groups: households dependent on agricultural minimum wages
claims.limitations: Global food/input price pressures also contributed; household counts are unspecified.

claims.paraphrase: IACHR reports Nicaragua’s 2025 legal changes weakened environmental safeguards and participation or consultation mechanisms in a context of high climate vulnerability.
claims.limitations: National conclusion; no specific climate event is linked to legal changes.
claims.source_stated_fcv_link: Para. 124 says weakened safeguards and consultation intensified a climate conducive to dispossession and collective-property violations.

claims.paraphrase: IACHR reports that TELCOR ordered closure and confiscation of Indigenous radios in Bilwi and Waspam; they covered 17 Mayangna and Miskitu territories and reported local violence and climate or environmental problems and effects.
claims.limitations: The report documents the radios’ stated roles and closure, not effects on preparedness or adaptation.
claims.source_stated_fcv_link: IACHR identifies the stations as channels for reporting violence and climate or environmental problems and effects; it does not assess downstream outcomes (para. 134).

claims.paraphrase: IACHR reports an armed-settler attack on Mayangna Alal (Sauni As, 30 km from Bonanza, Bosawás) in January 2020: at least four killed, over 16 homes burned, survival goods looted and 79 families displaced.
claims.limitations: This is conflict-driven displacement and asset loss; the report does not state a climate or weather connection.

claims.locator: Official announcement, paragraphs on launch and SINAREM functions (web page lines 25–35).
claims.paraphrase: SINAPRED announced SINAREM’s launch on 20 February 2025; the system is designed for real-time monitoring, early warning and response to disasters including floods.
claims.limitations: Launch and intended functions are reported, but operational coverage and performance are not evaluated.

claims.locator: WFP plan page, paragraphs on priorities and Outcomes 1–3.
claims.paraphrase: WFP’s 2024–2029 plan commits to integrated disaster-risk management, nutrition-sensitive social protection and school feeding linked to smallholder resilience, especially for women and climate-adaptive farming capacities.
claims.limitations: These are planned priorities and outcomes through 2029, not evidence of delivery or tested resilience gains; no subnational target is named.

search_audit.outcome: Opened the full IACHR thematic report; it documents land dispossession, armed-settler violence, displacement and radio shutdowns in named Caribbean Coast locations. No climate cause of violence is asserted.

search_audit.outcome: IACHR states that closed Indigenous radio channels had covered both violence and climate/environmental issues and effects; no downstream adaptation effect is inferred.

search_audit.query: Nicaragua resilience capacity adaptation early warning disaster risk management indigenous municipalities official 2024 2025 UN
search_audit.outcome: Directly opened the SINAPRED launch announcement and WFP strategic-plan summary. Both are institutional commitments/design; neither provides independent effectiveness results.

gaps: The IACHR annual chapter names 63 Dry Corridor municipalities but does not identify which municipalities or report local household rates; it does not attribute a particular event to climate change.
No inspected report attributes armed-settler violence or displacement to a climate hazard; the Dry Corridor and Caribbean Coast findings should not be combined into an inferred causal chain.

The IACHR documents climate/environment information and violence-reporting roles of closed Indigenous radios but does not assess effects on preparedness or adaptation. SINAREM is described at launch/design stage, without independent operational-coverage or effectiveness evidence.
WFP's linked plan PDF returned an anti-robot challenge; only the substantive publisher-page summary was inspected and used.
